text: （この件はここで進めてます: https://example.com/pr/4207）
note: The founding incident shape: a URL inside fullwidth parentheses. Greedy (what platforms do) swallows the closing bracket and the link leads nowhere.
Prose resumes after the ideographic full stop without a space.
Ideographic comma, then prose. Greedy swallows the rest of the clause.
Scanning resumes at the cut: the second of two comma-joined URLs is found, not deleted. Greedy, which never cuts, fuses the pair.
A parenthetical opening immediately after the URL. Reading the pair as balanced would swallow the bracket, its contents and the sentence.
BALANCED's documented loss: a path carrying literal fullwidth brackets is cut at the opening one. Such paths arrive percent-encoded often enough to survive, and fail visibly when they do not.

BALANCED's documented loss: real titles end in 。, and the cut URL may resolve to a different page. Pasted URLs are not percent-encoded, so this loss is real; GREEDY is the preset that preserves such paths.

text: 参考 https://ja.example.org/wiki/機動戦士ガンダム：閃光のハサウェイ

greedy: https://ja.example.org/wiki/機動戦士ガンダム：閃光のハサウェイ

note: BALANCED's documented loss: subtitle colons are everyday title characters, and the cut loses most of the path. Same family as the bracket loss; GREEDY preserves it.

BALANCED's documented loss in the other direction: its premise is the punctuation line, so prose resuming with a *letter* — the ubiquitous particle — is swallowed exactly as under GREEDY. Only STRICT survives this shape.
※ (Po) is not in the curated stop set (v0), so BALANCED swallows the annotation — pinned so that adding it later is a visible spec change, not drift. See SPEC.md "Known gaps".

text: 詳しくは https://ja.example.org/wiki/ドナルド・トランプ を参照
note: ・ (U+30FB) joins the parts of a compound name. Cutting there yields a URL that resolves to a different page — the invisible failure BALANCED refuses.
BALANCED's other documented loss: two URLs joined by ・ fuse into one. STRICT cuts at the joiner and, because scanning resumes at the cut, recovers both.

The flip side of resumed scanning, pinned deliberately: once a cut severs the remainder, that remainder is prose — and URL-shaped text inside it is found, even where the uncut candidate would have treated it as an embedded query value. Under GREEDY (no cut) the inner URL stays embedded.
U+2019 doubles as the apostrophe inside words. BALANCED keeps it for the same visible-failure reason as ・.

The cost of protecting L’Étranger, pinned: a URL closed by a curly quote swallows the quote and the prose after it. Its opening twin ‘ (U+2018) remains a stop — the pair is deliberately asymmetric; ‘'s stop behavior is pinned by the literal sweep in the test suite, since prose almost never places it directly after a URL.

text: 詳しくは https://ja.example.org/wiki/日本語 を参照
note: Fullwidth letters are not punctuation: BALANCED keeps them. STRICT is for sides that guarantee percent-encoded URLs.
ASCII closing brackets peel only when unbalanced; a matched pair belongs to the path.
A URL inside ASCII parentheses: the unmatched closer peels.
Sentence-ending ASCII punctuation peels from the tail.
A URL is quoted far more often than it ends in a quote.
The cost of the quote rule, stated: a query value ending in a quote loses it to the prose reading.

| is not a legal URL character unencoded under RFC 3986 (RFC 2396 filed it under characters that must be escaped), but query strings in the wild carry it bare. Escaping it for a platform's markup is adapter territory, not extent.
Dashboards emit brace-carrying URLs; the balanced pair survives the closer peel.
Not a legal URL character unencoded (RFC 2396 filed ^ under characters that must be escaped; RFC 3986 admits it nowhere), but dashboards emit it bare and platforms link it.
Percent-encoded fullwidth brackets (【】) pass every policy — the safe arrival form for the paths BALANCED cuts when literal.

text: 他说“详见 https://example.com/a”然后走了
note: Chinese curly closing quote right after the URL, prose continuing without a space.
The halfwidth corner bracket ｣ (U+FF63) is a stop too — the halfwidth kana block has its own punctuation.
Fullwidth exclamation ends the URL on sight.
Horizontal ellipsis (U+2026) reads as prose trailing off, not path.
U+3000 is whitespace: the candidate itself ends there, before any policy applies (its WIDE_STOP entry is defense in depth).
A fragment belongs to the URL and must survive whole.
Nothing but the scheme survives the peel: not a URL, no span.
The fullwidth twin of bare-scheme. The prose-trusting presets stop at 。 and drop the empty remainder; GREEDY, trusting everything, calls even this a URL — its nature, pinned.
Fullwidth colon before the URL is prose; the one after it ends the URL (for non-greedy readers).
Extents are decided per URL; order of appearance is preserved.

text: 旧リンク http://x.example/a、更新済み
note: Plain http is a candidate too.
RFC 3986 §3.1: schemes are case-insensitive, and platforms link HTTPS:// just the same. The extraction preserves the original casing.

A zero-width space baked into a URL looks identical to the real URL and is not — the invisible failure. The prose-trusting presets stop at copy-paste debris (see DEBRIS); GREEDY, true to its stance, keeps it.
STRICT's known sharp edge, pinned: ascii_only is code-point-level, so a combining mark cuts after its base letter and yields a plausible-but-different ASCII URL. Normalization is out of scope in v0.
Chat markup wraps URLs in emphasis markers; the closing marker peels so it is not baked into the link.

< and > never belong to a candidate — the old plain-text convention for delimiting URLs. Without that exclusion this URL would swallow >です; the brackets touch the URL here, so this case actually exercises the rule.
The tail peel removes trailing punctuation while it lasts — here both ! and ?.
